metadata.case_name: LAU MEI WA v. LI KING YIN AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: Her traumatic brain injury consisted of bifrontal cerebral contusion (bruising), high left parietal fracture, left occipital fracture, subdural haematoma, and traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage.
source: Her traumatic brain injury consisted of bifrontal cerebral contusion (bruising), high left parietal fracture, left occipital fracture, subdural haematoma, and traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage.

injuries.description: small left pneumothorax, multiple left rib fractures
source: Urgent CT scan brain, thorax, abdomen and pelvis showed traumatic brain injuries, small left pneumothorax, multiple left rib fractures, fracture left clavicle, fracture pelvis, fracture left ala and body of sacrum, and fracture anterior left acetabulum.

injuries.icd_description: Multiple fractures of lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: open scalp laceration and head contusions
source: She suffered head contusions, multiple fractures, multiple abrasions over her scalp/back, and an open scalp laceration.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: Major Depressive Episode / mild depression (psychiatric condition diagnosed post-Accident)
source: When seen by the clinical psychologist at WKPC on 3 June 2011, the plaintiff was noted to be a case of "mild depression, ?AN" referred for psychotherapy.
In summary, Dr Kwan concluded that the plaintiff suffered from Major Depressive Episode mild in severity (ICD-10) with no anxiety and psychotic symptoms.

injuries.description: anorexia nervosa and chronic laxative abuse with syncope, episodes of severe anaemia and low potassium level (pre-existing)
source: Medically, the plaintiff had anorexia nervosa and chronic laxative abuse with (a) syncope, episodes of severe anaemia and low potassium (K or K+) level, (b) severe hypokalaemia (ie K level 2.0 secondary to senokot overdose "~30tabs/day") requiring ICU admission in 2008, and (c) secondary amenorrhoea for several years.

manifestations.description: Generalised headache, experienced about once a week, occasionally woke her from sleep
Vertigo in early days after the Accident; left with brief attacks (minutes only) of light-headedness about twice a month
Nausea and vomiting about twice a month
Subjective impairment of memory and concentration; slow in taking in things and tended to forget them easily; loss of train of thought
Low/unstable mood, depression, anhedonia (getting little enjoyment out of life), lack of energy and motivation
Insomnia with nightmares and startle awakenings
Transient left sided weakness / left hemiplegia (noted with GCS deterioration to E4V2M6 and left hemiplegia on 17 October 2009 which later resolved)
Persistent occasional left chest wall pain and occasional pelvic/left hip/thigh pain
Dizziness on exertion and feeling of general malaise
Dependence on mother for some activities of daily living initially since she could not stand stably or walk without help (regained within first month)
Poor appetite / eating problems related to anorexia nervosa (pre-existing) with episodes of hypokalaemia and anaemia

treatments_received: sutures to scalp wound under local anaesthesia
urgent CT scans (brain, thorax, abdomen and pelvis)
blood transfusion (2 pints of packed cells)
fluid and electrolyte replacement including potassium replacement (slow K)
conservative treatment for rib fractures and pneumothorax (shoulder immobiliser)
clinical psychology intervention / stress reduction breathing
incision and debridement for left ankle abscess
left 4th metatarsal sequestrectomy, left tib posterior synovectomy and debridement with 10 gentamicin beads inserted
antibiotics (including gentamicin beads) and wound care
anti-TB drug (noted in Wound Assessment Form dated 9 January 2012)
treatments_future: vocational training / work capacity evaluation / rehabilitation (referred)

losses.description: Was dependent on her mother for some activities of daily living since she could not stand stably or walk without help (regained within first month).
Has not returned to work since the Accident; was unemployed at time of Accident and has not returned to work.
Stayed at home most of the time and went out less; rarely ventured outdoors except for medical appointments.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Dared not go out alone for fear of fainting in the street and needed to be accompanied.

When seen by the clinical psychologist at WKPC on 3 June 2011, the plaintiff was noted to be a case of "mild depression, ?AN" referred for psychotherapy. In summary, Dr Kwan concluded that the plaintiff suffered from Major Depressive Episode mild in severity (ICD-10) with no anxiety and psychotic symptoms.
